newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MAY 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - MAY 30.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The national economy ministry has given notice that inflation will fall dramatically to 5.2 or 5.1 percent in May, from 5.9 in April. National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou says the steady fall in inflation is an indicator of the stable course of the economy and is expected to contribute to stabilising the jittery currency market.
--OTE, Greece's telecoms organisation, will pay shareholders a dividend of 180 drachmas per share for 1996. The dividend for 1997 could reach 250 drachmas if the orgnisation makes its targets.
--The applications to settle outstanding taxation debts must be submitted by June 29, according to the finance ministry.

--The finance ministry is planning a new withdrawal of older-technology cars within the year. There are plans for these cars to be exported to non-EU countries, part of efforts to replace and revive the "fleet" and reduce environmental pollution.

--The drachma came under serious pressure yesterday resulting in the Bank of Greece intervening to keep the Ecu at 312 drachmas. There was also activity in forex outflows and interbank interest rates, but the bank says there's no cause for concern.
--Supporting the drachma's parity against the Ecu against the pressures it has received over the past week has cost almost one billion drachmas.

--Papandoniou's message to the ailing Agricultural Bank of Greece is blunt - privatise subsidiary firms, place others on the bourse for new share offers, develop a time-frame for restructuring and a possible date for the entry of the bank's shares on the bourse.

--The bill on the autonomy of the Bank of Greece will be discussed in Parliament soon, following its submission yesterday by Papantoniou. Once passed, the responsibility for exchange policy will rest in the hands of the central bank.
--Six major financial concerns - two Greek and four foreign - have expressed interest in the purchase of 51 perent of Greece's biggest poultry processor, Mimikos.
--Papantoniou says the Irish model of convergence - putting a lid on nominal wages and greater flexibility - is worthy of imitation.
